summary: Sangharakshita worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and under Chien Ming Chen, Jagdish Kashyap, Dhardo Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dudjom Rinpoche, later founding the Triratna Buddhist Community in 1967.

Sangseraima Ujeed is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford (~2013–2018) and held a Ho postdoctoral fellowship in Buddhist Studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~2018–2020).

Sangye Tenzin was a scholar of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who served as Abbot of Menri Monastery. A doctoral student attested at the University of Virginia in 2026, he taught Matthew T. Kapstein and Michael J. Sweet.

Sanjay Subrahmanyam works in history. Educated at St. Stephen's College, the Delhi School of Economics, and the University of Delhi, he held chairs at Oxford, the EHESS, UCLA (where he was founding director), and the Collège de France (2013–2021).
Sanjit Kumar Sadhukhan is an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under M. K. Ganguli (attested 1994) and traditional teacher A. P. Lama.

Sanjukta Gupta works in Indology and religious studies. She earned degrees from Calcutta, Visva-Bharati, and Utrecht (under Jan Gonda). She held posts at Visva-Bharati, Calcutta, Jadavpur (~1961–1967), Utrecht (~1967–1986), and Oxford (~1991).
Sanne Dokter-Mersch is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. She completed her PhD at Leiden University (~2016–2021) under the supervision of Peter C. Bisschop and Yuko Yokochi.

Sao Htun Hmat Win is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Harvard University and under Bhaddanta Narada. He taught at Rangoon University, headed research at the International Institute of Advanced Buddhistic Studies, and advised the Ministry of Religious Affairs.
Sara Frumento is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. She pursued a DPhil in Area Studies (South Asia) at the University of Oxford and Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2026).

Sara L. McClintock specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. She earned her PhD from Harvard (2002) and studied at Columbia, CIHTS, and Lausanne under Tom Tillemans and others. She held posts at Wisconsin-Madison and Emory University.
Sarah Aoife Richardson specializes in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Toronto in 2016 under the supervision of Jenny Purtle.

Sarah E. Fraser specializes in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Michigan and Kobe University, and held posts at Northwestern University (Associate Professor in 1996) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2000).

Sarah H. Jacoby is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Yale University and the University of Virginia (~1999–2007), and she held academic posts at Columbia University (2006–2009) and Northwestern University (2009).

Sarah Harding works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche (1972) and Lama Tenpa, served as a fellow at the Tsadra Foundation (~2000), and taught at Naropa University (~1992–2018).

Sarah J. Horton specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein and held a post as Assistant Professor at Macalester College (attested 2006).
Sarah Merkle-Schneider is an Indologist who completed her M.A. studies and holds an M.A. post at the University of Tübingen (attested 2026).

Sarah Shaw is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Lance S. Cousins. She held affiliations with Oxford's Faculty of Oriental Studies, Wolfson College, and the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies.
Saraju Rath is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who held posts at the International Institute for Asian Studies, attested in 2012 and 2022.

Sarasi Kumar Saraswati worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Sivaprasad Bhattacharyya and Jitendra Nath Banerjea, served as Librarian at The Asiatic Society in 1943, and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Sarat Chandra Das worked in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and Presidency College, Chennai. He was director of Bhutia Boarding School (1874) and Tibetan translator for the Government of Bengal (1881–1904).
